summary.headline: Websol H1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR 734 crore (+89.6% YoY) and Q2 revenue rose 114.6% to INR 361 crore, with EBITDA of INR 128 crore in the quarter.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the strongest half-year on record, with revenue of INR 734 crore and EBITDA of INR 254 crore in H1. Q2 revenue rose 114.6% YoY to INR 361 crore, EBITDA rose 77.3% to INR 128 crore and net profit rose 73.2% to INR 80 crore. The company repaid its IREDA debt in August and is now debt-free, with cash from operations of INR 244 crore in H1. Management also announced a 4 GW integrated greenfield project at Falta (West Bengal), a TOPCon conversion, and entry into EPC, IPP, solar parks and energy trading.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 132 crore in H1 FY26

segments.name: Solar cells (Falta plant)
segments.commentary: Cell line ran at 91% utilisation in Q2, producing a little over 255 MW of cells. Current cell capacity is 1.2 GW (Mono PERC).

segments.name: Solar modules
segments.commentary: Module capacity utilisation was 68% in Q2 on 550 MW of capacity. All modules are DCR and ALMM compliant, per management.

segments.name: Websol Renewables (new subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Will house the 2 GW TOPCon integrated cell and module line; Vinay appointed CEO. Board approved EPC, solar IPP, solar parks and energy trading, with 40% stake in Bright Earth Cell Pvt Ltd for trading. Revenue not yet expected; described as early stage.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to stabilise around 30% in FY27 (H1 FY27 stated at 35%); some moderation expected as new capex comes on. No FY28-29 margin guidance given.
Mono PERC to TOPCon conversion (600 MW to 750 MW TOPCon line) targeted for commercialisation by March 2027; cell capacity to reach 1.35 GW and module capacity 550 MW by end FY27.

First 2 GW phase of 4 GW Falta greenfield integrated facility: project cost INR 1,350 crore; trial runs targeted Q3 FY28 (management also said December 2027); civil construction from January 2027 (per Q&A).
Ingot-wafer backward integration planned; management referenced June 2028 as the working timeline, contingent on ALMM List-III clarity. Capex to be confirmed by next quarter.

Funding: management says equity (about INR 400-500 crore from internal accruals) with the balance as debt; debt split targeted at roughly 30:70 equity:debt, though the Q&A also said 50:50 is feasible.
capex_capacity: Falta TOPCon conversion: 600 MW Mono PERC line converted to 750 MW TOPCon, adding 150 MW; cost about INR 270 crore; equipment ordered and largely shipped, civil and utility work ongoing; funding from internal accruals with possible leverage.

Greenfield integrated facility at Falta, West Bengal: 54.2 acres allotted at Falta Industrial Park; 4 GW total in two 2 GW phases; first phase cost INR 1,350 crore; land development to finish by early next year.
Wafer and ingot to be set up at a separate facility, not on the 54.2-acre site; capex not yet finalised.
Current capacity: 1.2 GW cells (Mono PERC), 550 MW modules; cell utilisation 91%, module utilisation 68% in Q2.
demand_pricing: Management cited about 30.8 GW of Indian solar capacity added in H1 FY27, described as the highest six-month installation. It also cited about 20 GW of cell capacity additions in the first six months, but said additions have been lower than expected.
Order book at end Q2 FY27 stood at INR 1,280 crore.
Management said a cell-to-module supply gap persists, and the ALMM List-II deadline extension was cited as evidence of insufficient domestic cell capacity.
TOPCon cell realisations are higher than Mono PERC; management estimated the gap at around 1 cent per watt (the transcript says 'cent', so the unit is unclear), without quantifying it further.
Silver price moderation and silver-use optimisation helped blended margins.

qa_highlights.question: Detailed timeline and financing plan for the 4 GW West Bengal project?
qa_highlights.answer: Two phases of 2 GW each; first phase cost INR 1,350 crore; equity from internal accruals and the balance as debt; land development to finish by early next year, with trial runs targeted in Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the role of the new CEO for the renewables business, and when will the subsidiary operate?
qa_highlights.answer: Vinay appointed CEO of Websol Renewables, which will run the 2 GW TOPCon integrated line; operations expected in Q3 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 4 GW expansion plan on track, and what is the ALMM List-III plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Ingot-wafer project is in technical evaluation and awaits ALMM List-III timeline clarity; June 2028 is the current working timeline. Capex to be confirmed by next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter BESS?
qa_highlights.answer: No firm plans yet; the company is evaluating BESS and will update investors once there is clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any equity or warrant issue planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No equity raise or warrants decided; expansion is to be funded from internal accruals and current funds, with a second-market equity raise only if required.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin of 35%; expected to stabilise around 30% this year, with some moderation as new capacity comes on. No FY28-29 number given.

qa_highlights.question: Does China's technology export restriction affect the TOPCon and 4 GW plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Restrictions cover certain furnaces; alternative suppliers are outside China. The TOPCon line supplier is German and the 4 GW plan is also sourced outside China, and no turnkey line was ordered from a Chinese company.

qa_highlights.question: Can the 2 GW phase be funded 50:50 equity and debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is 30:70 equity to debt to keep leverage capacity for further capex (2 GW more, wafer-ingot); 50:50 is feasible, per management.

risks_watch: Project timelines are tight: construction begins around January 2027 and trial runs are targeted for Q3 FY28, while the TOPCon conversion must be commercialised by March 2027.
EBITDA margin is expected to moderate from 35% in H1 toward about 30% as new capacity comes on; FY28-29 margins not guided.
Ingot-wafer capex and funding are unconfirmed and depend on ALMM List-III timelines; management has also said the wafer project's funding may need equity.
Debt funding for the 2 GW greenfield project (about INR 945-1,000 crore of debt on the 70:30 plan) is not yet secured, per the Q&A; the TOPCon upgrade may also use leverage.
Chinese technology export restrictions: management says current exposure is limited, but future equipment sourcing should be monitored.
New EPC, IPP, solar park and energy trading businesses are at an early stage with no revenue guidance; the Bright Earth Cell 40% stake is a related investment to monitor.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and on the operating and cash-flow record, with the company debt-free after the IREDA repayment. Cautious and evasive on forward items: no FY28-29 margin guidance, no BESS or wafer capex figures, and no EPC/IPP revenue estimates. Several funding answers shifted between 30:70 and 50:50 equity-debt splits.
key_quotes: We are moving from a 600 megawatt line to a planned 750 megawatt of TOPCon line, which is targeted towards the end of this financial year.
H1 FY27 marked Websol's highest ever half-yearly revenue and operating profit, with revenue reaching INR 734 crores and EBITDA stood at INR 254 crores.
So we are, you know, so we are not constrained by the Chinese restrictions.
We are, we are a debt-free company with a net worth of INR780 crores, and we believe that the cash accrual will be healthy in the coming future.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 35% but management guided FY27 to stabilise around 30%, with moderation as new capex comes on; no FY28-29 margin guidance given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 150 MW TOPCon conversion at Falta (600 MW to 750 MW, INR 270 crore, equipment largely shipped) targets commercialisation by March 2027; first 2 GW greenfield phase (INR 1,350 crore, approved) has trial runs targeted Q3 FY28 (also cited as December 2027), though timelines are inconsistent across sources.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Cell line ran at 91% utilisation in Q2 (about 255 MW), the INR 1,280 crore order book supports volumes, and cell capacity rises to 1.35 GW by end FY27; module utilisation of 68% on 550 MW leaves spare module headroom.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: Q4 FY27 (wafer capex to be confirmed)
rows.why: Cell utilisation at 91% with the 4 GW Falta project already approved, and ingot-wafer capex to be confirmed by next quarter, so further capex announcements are already under way.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin down to about 30% from 35% in H1, and there is no explicit revenue or volume guidance raise in the call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin guided to moderate from 35% to about 30%, and the greenfield timeline has slipped toward December 2027 with construction starting January 2027 and debt for the 2 GW phase (about INR 945-1,000 crore) not yet secured.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TOPCon cells (750 MW line) are targeted for commercialisation by March 2027, with TOPCon realisations higher than Mono PERC by about 1 cent per watt per management.

rows.label: Order book INR 1,280 crore at end Q2 FY27
rows.why: Order book of INR 1,280 crore against H1 revenue of INR 734 crore gives roughly 1.7x half-year revenue cover, supporting near-term execution.

rows.label: Debt-free after IREDA repayment in August
rows.why: IREDA debt repaid in August 2026 with H1 cash from operations of INR 244 crore, though the 2 GW greenfield phase will add about INR 945-1,000 crore of debt on the 70:30 plan.

rows.label: Renewables subsidiary: EPC, IPP, solar parks, energy trading
rows.why: Board approved new businesses and Websol Renewables (CEO Vinay) will run the 2 GW TOPCon line with operations in Q3 FY28, but no revenue is expected yet and the business is early stage.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the cash-flow record and being debt-free, but cautious on forward margins (guided down to about 30%), wafer capex and funding, where the equity-debt split shifted between 30:70 and 50:50; analysts probed the timeline, funding and China equipment exposure.
